comments.author: name_was_taken
comments.body:
So far, my experience has been that they're all *about* the same, and about the time you find that one is better than the rest, the others have an update and catch up.

I would recommend looking at the engine first, and deciding if it can do the game you want, and how easily, regardless of AI.  More documentation and community posting is better, both for AI and non-AI developers.

To me, that indicates that Unity is still a really strong choice for inexperienced developers, despite all their crazy mis-steps.

That said, I've chosen Godot.  It's free, it's Free, and it's pretty freaking good for 3D since about 4.4.  (And for 2D since 3.x)

comments.author: AwayMatter
comments.body:
I really like Cursor. Overall, there wont be much of a difference as the bulk of the work is done by the model not the IDE. In fact, cli tools like Codex cli or Claude code can often get better results. I love Cursor for their tab autocompletes, the best out there imo.

Roo code is an extension for vscode based IDEs (Windsurf, cursor, vscode itself) that I really liked too. If already pay for a ChatGPT sub, try the codex cli. You get decent weekly limits with the 20$ plan that may be going to waste, and 5-Codex is a good model.

comments.author: alokin_09
comments.body: Kilo Code should fit your use case. Pair it with newer-gen LLMs (e.g., Supernova) for the heavy lifts. FWIW I’m working with the Kilo Code team and have seen folks get solid results with that combo.
